scope: Selected UL and FM Approvals counterfeit-mark and falsified-certificate alerts for fire sprinklers, worldwide. These are not recalls. Authentic products bearing a copied designation are not implicated. Not exhaustive.
verification: Every record's original notice was downloaded and read on 2026-10-18. Cues are paraphrased; open source_url for photos.
known_gaps: UL 18PN-07 (PS002, Indonesia) cited by UL 18PN-19; not reviewed.
UL 15PN-21 (TY3151/TY3251, Vietnam) cited by UL 18PN-20; not reviewed.
FM GN5651 alert dated 2006-09-15, referenced by later Globe alerts; not in the current FM listing; not reviewed.
UL's public-notice directory lists sprinkler notices from 2018 onward only; earlier UL notices may exist.

field_guide.external_cues: Issuer-stated differences from authentic units, or self-evident inconsistencies, visible on an installed unit in a close, sharp photo. One is enough for Suspect counterfeit features.
field_guide.supporting_cues: Finish, color, font, stamp-depth or identifying-marking observations. Alone they support only a Counterfeit alert lead.
field_guide.other_markings: Identifying markings the issuer printed; used as lookup keys. Genuine units can carry them, so a marking counts only when it also appears in that record's external_cues or supporting_cues.
field_guide.removed_unit_cues: Needs a removed unit or verified spare (inlet, seal, threads, internal parts). Never ask anyone to remove or open an installed sprinkler to check these.
field_guide.non_discriminators: Features the issuer says do not separate authentic from counterfeit.
field_guide.photo_resolvable: yes = external cues usually decide; partial = only supporting or some removed-unit cues; no = document alert, or the issuer published markings without an authentic comparison.

cross_alert_statements.statement: No current FM Approved sprinklers use O-ring seals.
cross_alert_statements.use: Removed-unit cue on a modern FM-marked unit (FM notes O-ring seals were in general use until about 2001). An alert's O-ring statement does not establish O-ring construction for the unit in hand, so it does not trigger the O-ring Risk flag.

cross_alert_statements.statement: No FM Approved sprinklers use Job model F5 bulbs; FM Approved Job 5 mm bulbs are G5.
cross_alert_statements.use: For the models FM names, Job F5 is a stated difference from the authentic model whether or not an FM mark is present (as of the alert dates): Tyco TY3151/TY3251 (2016, 2017; also UL 14PN-9), Globe GL5651/GL5661/GL5653 (2008, 2009, 2017, 2018) and Viking VK100 (2014). On any other FM-marked model it is a lead (FM's 2011 and 2012 wording says 'currently'). On other models without an FM mark it is not a cue; genuine Job F5 bulbs exist.
cross_alert_statements.strength: external for named models; supporting on other FM-marked units

cross_alert_statements.statement: No FM Approved sprinklers use bulbs marked YDϕ5.
cross_alert_statements.use: Strong cue on units marked Tyco or Globe or bearing an FM mark (FM 2017, 2019); otherwise a pointer to read the alert.
cross_alert_statements.strength: external for Tyco, Globe or FM-marked units

cross_alert_statements.statement: Any GL5651 dated 2022 or later that is also marked GLOBE can be assumed counterfeit.
Bulb markings seen only on counterfeits in these alerts: ATOP⌀5 / ATOP Ø5, YDϕ5 / YD05, YH-5, CDGIX.
cross_alert_statements.use: Strong cue on units marked Tyco or Globe or bearing an FM mark (FM 2009, 2017, 2019, 2025: authentic bulbs are Job G5, Geissler G or, for GL5601, Job F3/N3); otherwise a pointer to read the alert. D77447 is left out: UL lists it with counterfeit-printed Job G5 text and it may be a copied lot code.
cross_alert_statements.strength: external for Tyco, Globe or FM-marked units
